newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-DUVAL TAKES FIRST-ROUND LEAD IN TEXAS GOLF.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-DUVAL TAKES FIRST-ROUND LEAD IN TEXAS GOLF.

text.p: David Duval, still
searching for his first victory after four years on the PGA
Tour, took a two-stroke lead after the first-round at the $1.6
million Houston Open.
Duval took advantage of good scoring conditions in early
morning play to finish with a 65, two shots ahead of Curtis
Strange.
The sun came out and winds picked up in the afternoon,
sending the scores upwards before large crowds.
Strange, a three-time winner in Houston, is seeking his
first victory since back-to-back U.S. Open victories in
Australian Grant Waite heads a group of five players tied
for third at 68.
Australian native and Houston resident Steve Elkington is
among seven players at 69. Also in the group where defending
champion Mark Brooks and former U.S. Masters champion Fred
Couples.
After birdies on holes 4-5-6 and 14-15-16, Duval said he
was pleased with his opening-round play.
"I wouldn't say it was as easy as all that," Duval said.
"You know, you have those days where you play well. I hit the
ball a lot better than I have, but we still have a long way to
go."
Strange has spent as much time in the television
announcing booth as the golf course in the last couple of
years.
After bogeying the par-5 first hole, Strange got his round
jump-started with an eagle two at the par-4 fourth hole. He
holed a 161-yard fairway shot with a six iron.
"I played a whole lot better than I've been playing,"
Strange said. "One round doesn't turn my game around, but I
keep thinking it's got to turn around somewhere."
Strange toured the back nine in 32 strokes, with birdies
on holes 11-12, 15 and 18, where he stroked in a 12-foot putt.
Strange's last professional win came at the 1993 Greg
Norman Holden Classic in Australia.
